segments.t: DE
AI assistantKTPH000

KorTTY can analyze selected terminal text with an OpenAI-compatible AI endpoint, an integrated local llama.cpp model, or a configured local CLI and open the answer in a temporary AI result tab. You can also start agent-style workflows to automate SSH tasks or get plans reviewed before implementation.

When KTPH000Configuration KTPH002 Prevent System SleepKTPH001 is enabled on macOS or Windows, korTTY keeps the computer awake while an AI API, local-model, web-tool, or local AI CLI request is waiting for a result. The assertion is released after the last concurrent AI request finishes; if no terminal is connected and no future or running Scheduler job exists, the computer may then sleep normally. Display sleep remains available.
KTPH000
Data Security

Selected terminal text is transmitted to the configured AI service for analysis. That text can contain sensitive information such as credentials, hostnames, file paths, stack traces, or other operational details. For sensitive data, use an KTPH000integrated local GGUF modelKTPH001 or another endpoint you trust. Embedded inference uses an authenticated loopback-only server; remote providers receive the reviewed request over the network. If you provide an KTPH002API KeyKTPH003, korTTY stores it encrypted with your master password.
SetupKTPH000
Open KTPH000Edit KTPH002 Global SettingsKTPH001.
Go to KTPH000AIKTPH001.

Create one or more AI profiles in KTPH000Settings KTPH010 AIKTPH001 or KTPH002AI KTPH011 AI Manager KTPH012 ProfilesKTPH003. Choose KTPH004HTTP APIKTPH005, KTPH006Local CLIKTPH007, or KTPH008Integrated llama.cppKTPH009 as the connection mode.

For HTTP profiles, enter an API URL, model, and optional encrypted API key. For an embedded profile, select an installed GGUF model; korTTY supplies the private endpoint and temporary key. Use KTPH000AI Manager KTPH002 Local ModelsKTPH001 first when no GGUF is installed.

Optionally configure KTPH000Prompt optimizationKTPH001, KTPH002Max charactersKTPH003, KTPH004TokenizerKTPH005, KTPH006Token limitKTPH007, warning thresholds, token reset cycle, supported KTPH008ReasoningKTPH009 effort, and KTPH010Internet accessKTPH011 per profile. korTTY exposes reasoning choices based on the configured endpoint and model; LM Studio's exact native capability metadata takes precedence over compatibility probes so a silently converted effort is not shown as supported. Profiles without a supported explicit reasoning mode keep provider-default behavior.

Optionally set an KTPH000AI request timeoutKTPH001 in minutes. korTTY does not time out AI requests on its own, so a long task such as the snippet editor's KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 runs until the model answers. The value on the KTPH004ProfilesKTPH005 page applies to every profile; KTPH006Timeout for this profileKTPH007 overrides it for a single profile, and 0 there means that profile never times out. See KTPH008AI settingsKTPH009.
Click KTPH000Test AI ConnectionKTPH001.
Optionally choose a KTPH000Default profileKTPH001, then assign separate Text/translation and Coding roles under KTPH002AI Manager KTPH004 Local AIKTPH003. An empty role uses the default profile.

Optionally configure the default language for AI-generated text inside code comments and program output, enable the extra instructions field for snippet AI actions, and set how many alternative solutions the snippet editor should request.

Optionally configure the terminal-agent input-history size (default 20, range 5–100), the agent command name, case-insensitive command matching, execution target, prompt-hook usage, per-run setup dialog, debug/runtime visibility, and activity-panel preferences for KTPH000AI AgentKTPH001 and KTPH002AI PlanningKTPH003.
Optionally disable the confirmation dialog for KTPH000SummarizeKTPH001 and KTPH002Solve ProblemKTPH003 if you want a faster workflow. KTPH004AskKTPH005 always opens the prompt dialog.
AI Profile Setup WizardKTPH000
A guided wizard creates AI profiles with support for both local and cloud-based language models.
To open the wizard:
KTPH000Settings KTPH006 AIKTPH001, click KTPH002Add ProfileKTPH003 or KTPH004EditKTPH005 an existing profile.
KTPH000Tools KTPH004 AI Manager KTPH005 ProfilesKTPH001, click KTPH002AddKTPH003.
The wizard guides you through:
KTPH000Connection TypeKTPH001 - Choose local LM Studio or a cloud provider.
KTPH000LM Studio SetupKTPH001 - If local: pick a loaded LM Studio model from the list or use KTPH002AutoKTPH003 mode.
KTPH000Cloud Provider SetupKTPH001 - If cloud: select the provider (Anthropic Claude API, OpenAI, or other OpenAI-compatible endpoint).

KTPH000API DetailsKTPH001 - Enter API Key and select or enter the Model name — the model list is pre-filled with common models for the chosen provider, and KTPH002Load modelsKTPH003 merges the endpoint's live model list on top. Optionally configure Reasoning effort (if the provider/model supports extended thinking).
KTPH000Profile NameKTPH001 - Enter a display name for the profile (e.g., "Claude Opus", "Local LM Studio").
Native Anthropic (Claude) API support is included alongside existing OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

For fully integrated GGUF inference, use the separate KTPH000AI Manager KTPH004 Local Models KTPH005 Setup assistantKTPH001. It checks hardware, recommends Text/Coding/embedding models, reviews license and exact size, verifies the immutable download, creates an embedded profile, assigns the selected role, and runs a real local chat or embedding function test. See KTPH002Local models with llama.cppKTPH003.
Model selectionKTPH000
The model selector in KTPH000Settings KTPH004 AIKTPH001 and KTPH002Tools KTPH005 AI Manager KTPH006 ProfilesKTPH003 is editable:

For known cloud providers the dropdown is pre-filled with common model names for the configured endpoint, so a concrete model can be chosen without an API key. The refresh button next to the selector merges the endpoint's live KTPH000 list on top when the API key is valid.
Choosing a listed model stores it as the manual selection.
Typing a model name stores it as the manual selection so any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works.

KTPH000AutoKTPH001 is offered only for local LM Studio endpoints, where korTTY can actually detect the loaded model. Cloud profiles need a concrete model; if none is selected, requests stop with an explicit "select a specific AI model" error.
An KTPH001Integrated llama.cppKTPH002 profile lists installed model IDs from KTPH000; it does not use the HTTP URL or manual cloud-model field.
Role routing, RAG, and prompt orderKTPH000

korTTY classifies its own action types deterministically without asking a model. Translation, summary, problem solving, questions, prose descriptions, and AI ASCII-art pictures use the Text role; coding, completion, snippet review, security fixes, diagrams, and workflow generation use the Coding role. An explicit profile choice, security-check profile, or connection-specific profile takes precedence, followed by the role profile and then the default.

When matching knowledge stores are assigned to the request's Text or Coding role, an ordinary AI request is assembled in this order: korTTY's action/output contract, selected AI Skills, bounded untrusted RAG context with KTPH000 source markers, the resolved model-family preset, and finally the provider transport. Only retrieved excerpts are added, not the complete knowledge store; choosing a cloud profile sends those excerpts to that provider, so the knowledge-store role/profile assignment is the explicit disclosure decision. Strict JSON and code-payload rules remain authoritative. The dedicated source-only diagram request used by snippets and workflows is a narrow exception: after its fixed output contract korTTY always adds one compact, immutable action skill for the requested diagram family (logical-structure flowchart, sequence, state, class, or ER) and omits every configurable library skill and retrieval context. For a profile with a fixed model selection, korTTY automatically sets the request-scoped KTPH003ReasoningKTPH004 value to KTPH001 only when that value is available, without changing the saved profile. The action skill is not one of the 39 shipped configurable built-in skills: users cannot disable or edit it, and it adds no matching/classification request. The Full code analysis stages that apply selected improvements and its security-fix follow-up use the same fixed-model rule because they return bounded, machine-parsed full-script replacements; the preceding analysis still uses the profile's configured Reasoning value. An Auto profile is not overridden from previously discovered capabilities because its loaded model can change; an explicitly configured KTPH002 value still applies. Autonomous Agent, Planning, Swarm, and scheduled prompts require explicit RAG opt-in. See KTPH005RAG knowledge storesKTPH006 for the retrieval and privacy details.
Local LM Studio model selectionKTPH000

For local LM Studio profiles, korTTY can discover currently loaded LLM model keys and exact reasoning options through LM Studio's KTPH000 endpoint. A binary model that reports only KTPH001 and KTPH002 therefore no longer shows the Minimal, Low, Medium, High, or Extra high levels as supported merely because LM Studio would silently convert an unsupported value; an explicit KTPH003 request switches this feature off, while omitting the reasoning parameter uses the model's published default.

Auto mode resolves the effective model immediately before connection tests, AI chat and follow-up requests, terminal AI actions, and Terminal AI Agent runs. If exactly one LLM is loaded, korTTY uses that model. If multiple LLMs are loaded, korTTY uses the saved preferred model only when that model is currently loaded. If no LLM is loaded, or multiple LLMs are loaded without a valid saved preference, korTTY stops the request with an explicit error instead of guessing.
AI internet accessKTPH000
Internet access is configured per AI profile. Existing and new profiles default to KTPH000DisabledKTPH001.
Mode
Behavior
KTPH000DisabledKTPH001
No web tools or MCP integrations are sent with AI requests.
KTPH000KorTTY Tavily ToolKTPH001
korTTY adds a KTPH000 tool to eligible OpenAI-compatible KTPH001 requests. Tool calls are executed by korTTY through KTPH002.
KTPH000LM Studio Tavily MCPKTPH001
korTTY sends an LM Studio native KTPH000 request with a Tavily MCP integration.
KTPH000Bright Data Web MCPKTPH001
korTTY sends an LM Studio native KTPH000 request with a Bright Data MCP integration.
KTPH000Brave Search MCPKTPH001
korTTY sends an LM Studio native KTPH000 request with a configured Brave Search MCP plugin ID.
KTPH000SearXNG MCPKTPH001
korTTY sends an LM Studio native KTPH000 request with a configured SearXNG MCP plugin ID.
KTPH000LM Studio ToolpackKTPH001
korTTY sends an LM Studio native KTPH000 request with the configured LM Studio Toolpack MCP plugin ID.

Required provider configuration is entered under KTPH000Settings KTPH002 AI KTPH003 Internet tool configurationKTPH001. API keys and tokens are stored encrypted with the master password. MCP server labels and plugin IDs are stored as normal settings.
Important behavior:
Snippet AI, text correction, translation, snippet descriptions, alternative-solution requests, and AI ASCII-art generation do not use internet access.
Direct korTTY web tools have a 5-second connect timeout, a 20-second request timeout, and a maximum of two web-tool rounds per AI request.
LM Studio MCP requests with internet access use a longer total request timeout because the MCP server runs behind LM Studio.
Canceling a running request interrupts the Java HTTP request where the active provider supports interruption.

Tool errors are returned to the model as structured data. If the web tool times out, fails authentication, returns no results, or reaches the tool-round limit, the model is instructed to say that explicitly and not invent web facts.

For terminal-agent JSON planning, korTTY offers web tools only when the user task clearly asks for current or external information. Local file/script review tasks should be handled by shell commands such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, or test commands, not by web search.
AI SkillsKTPH000

AI Skills are reusable local instruction blocks that korTTY can add to AI requests. Use them for persistent preferences such as coding standards, review rules, operational policies, or language-specific style guidance.

Rendering details and requirements
SVG and rendered Mermaid output is displayed with JavaScript disabled and scripts/event handlers stripped from the document.
Mermaid 11.17.2 runs with its KTPH000 security level from a SHA-256-pinned local bundle; LaTeX is typeset by a separately loaded local MathJax bundle. Neither needs internet access.

Chat Mermaid retains the full bundled diagram support, including flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, mindmap, and architecture diagrams. Frontmatter, directives, network/file/data/JavaScript URLs, external images/icons, links, and click callbacks are rejected; source, edge-count, raster-size, and timeout limits protect the renderer.
Full LaTeX documents (KTPH000) intentionally stay code blocks; only formulas are typeset.
Mermaid follows the active chat's light/dark palette; other rendered images and formulas retain a readable neutral canvas.

The built-in manual (KTPH002Help KTPH012 ManualKTPH003, KTPH004KTPH000KTPH005) includes an AI-powered search. How it works:

korTTY selects the most relevant sections from the bundled offline manual (no embeddings, no external search service) and sends only those excerpts together with your question to your KTPH000default AI profileKTPH001.
The answer is generated KTPH000exclusively from the manual contentKTPH001 and is written in the app language. If the manual does not cover the question, the assistant says so instead of guessing.

If nothing in the manual matches the question, korTTY answers locally without contacting the AI endpoint at all.
Requirements:
A configured AI profile (see KTPH000SetupKTPH001); the default profile is used.
An unlocked master-password vault when the profile stores an encrypted API key.
Data Security

The question text and the selected manual excerpts are transmitted to the configured AI endpoint. The manual content itself is public documentation, but your question is free text — avoid pasting secrets into it, or use a trusted local endpoint such as KTPH000LM StudioKTPH001. Internet access modes are always disabled for manual questions.

How the AI Agent worksKTPH000
The Terminal AI Agent is a controlled terminal automation workflow. It does not run arbitrary model output directly in the interactive terminal. Instead, each turn follows this pattern:

korTTY probes the active SSH or local-shell session with a non-interactive command and records compact context such as current user, host, operating system, active terminal working directory, sudo availability, disk path, and recent command state.
korTTY sends the user task, probe snapshot, previous command results, active AI Skills, and optionally web-tool availability to the selected AI profile.
The model must return a strict JSON decision: run commands, ask for confirmation, finish, or block.
korTTY validates the JSON schema and command constraints. Invalid responses are repaired once; unsafe or unsupported command decisions are rejected.

korTTY runs approved commands through the active backend: SSH exec channels for SSH sessions or fresh local processes for local shells. Each command starts in the directory captured for the run. A KTPH000 inside one command does not persist to the next command.
Command output is added to the activity panel and to the next model turn until the task is complete, blocked, canceled, or the turn limit is reached.
Suitable tasksKTPH000
The agent is suitable for:
inspecting files, directories, package state, logs, service state, and system configuration;
creating or modifying scripts and configuration files when the task asks for it;
running tests, syntax checks, linters, or read-only diagnostic commands;
summarizing command output and explaining findings;
planning multi-step operational changes before implementation.
The agent is not intended for:
interactive full-screen programs such as KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, or commands that wait for prompts;
long-running daemons or commands without clear completion;
secret exfiltration or blind destructive commands;
web research for local files unless you explicitly ask for external/current information.

Safety and failure handlingKTPH000
korTTY adds guardrails around agent execution:
Commands are limited per turn and must be non-interactive.
Commands that change the system or require privilege can be routed through confirmation depending on settings and model decision.
Sudo uses KTPH000 and activity-panel password prompts. korTTY does not allow KTPH001, KTPH002, or commands that wait indefinitely for a terminal password prompt.

SSH directories are tracked from shell hooks, terminal prompt context, and probe results; if a tracked remote directory no longer exists, korTTY retries the probe from the SSH default directory and reports the issue. Local runs refresh the shell process directory or use an absolute native prompt path, freeze the result for the run, and stop safely when a changed directory cannot be determined or mapped.

While a terminal-targeted run is active, normal typing is still allowed; only run-control keys (++Esc++/++Ctrl+C++ to cancel the selected run, ++Ctrl+R++ to toggle its thinking details) are intercepted.
Web-search failures, HTTP errors, authentication errors, empty results, and timeouts are surfaced as explicit tool errors.
If the AI response does not match the required JSON schema, korTTY asks for a repair. If repair also fails, the run is blocked with an explanation.
